question: Why did the p95 latency go up on 16 March 2026?

contributing_factors.description: The deployment of catalog v3.20 likely caused the increase in p95 latency.
why_chain: The deployment of catalog v3.20 introduced changes that affected the system's performance.
The change in catalog v3.20 led to a rise in request volume, which in turn increased p95 latency.
The rise in request volume caused the autoscaler to scale out, leading to increased latency.

contributing_factors.description: The error rate increase could be a symptom of the underlying issues.
why_chain: The error rate increase could be due to the deployment of catalog v3.20.
The deployment of catalog v3.20 may have introduced bugs or changes that affected error handling.
The bugs or changes led to an increase in error rate, which could be a symptom of the underlying issues.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The increase in p95 latency was due to a configuration change.
ruled_out.reason: No evidence supports a configuration change as the cause of the increase in p95 latency.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The increase in p95 latency was due to a dependency issue with an external service.
ruled_out.reason: No evidence supports a dependency issue with an external service as the cause of the increase in p95 latency.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The increase in p95 latency was due to a sudden increase in network traffic.
ruled_out.reason: The increase in request volume and error rate are more likely causes than a sudden increase in network traffic.

evidence.summary: P95 latency for region us-east rose from 137 ms to 270 ms (+97%), with a change point at 2026-03-16T04:40:00Z.
The change is concentrated in region us-east: 4 of 12 service/region segments changed; the other segments stayed flat (largest after/before ratio 1.02).
At the same time, request volume for region us-east rose (2707 per 5 min before, 10491 per 5 min after, +288%).
At the same time, error rate for region us-east rose (0.40% before, 0.78% after, +97%).
Request volume 3x normal in us-east (us-east; 12 min after the change; record R009)
Deployed catalog v3.20 to us-east (routine release) (catalog, us-east; 126 min before the change; record R008)
autoscaler: scaling out, 4 new instances requested (us-east; 20 min after the change; record R010)

reasons: ✗ The closest change event is 126 min before the change, too far to be convincing.
✓ 2 log/alert record(s) after the change agree with the numbers.
✗ Request volume also rose, so a traffic explanation is still open.
✓ No competing change event fits as well.
✓ The main factor rests on this event.
missing_data: Change records from the hour before the change

actions.action: Roll back the catalog v3.20 deployment to revert the changes introduced by the deployment.
Monitor the system closely for any further changes or issues related to the catalog v3.20 deployment.
Review and optimize the autoscaler configuration to ensure it scales appropriately under normal and increased load conditions.
